Opulence

OP-yoo-lens -- from Latin opulentia, rooted in ops ('wealth, power'). · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Opulence is great wealth, richness, or luxury, especially as visibly displayed.

Visitors to the newly restored opera house gasped at its opulence, from the gold-leafed balconies to the velvet-lined private boxes.

Worked Example

The hotel lobby's marble columns, gold fixtures, and crystal chandeliers announced its opulence before a single guest reached the front desk.

Marble, gold, and crystal are all obvious, expensive signs of wealth and luxury -- exactly what opulence describes.

How Opulence Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

luxury

luxury: great comfort provided by expensive and beautiful things

lavishness

lavishness: the quality of being extremely generous or elaborate

Antonyms

squalor

squalor: extreme dirtiness caused by poverty or neglect

austerity

austerity: severe plainness and simplicity, often by necessity

How Strong Is It? — luxury → opulence → lavishness

luxury vs. opulence

luxury vs. opulence: Luxury is weaker than opulence: a hot bath after a week of camping is a small luxury, while opulence is heavier — wealth piled up and displayed on every surface.

lavishness vs. opulence

lavishness vs. opulence: Lavishness goes further than opulence: an opulent home displays its riches, but a wedding with ice sculptures, a live orchestra, and fireworks pushes into lavishness — spending so extreme it overflows all limits.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — op-

root — op-: wealth, power (Latin (ops))

suffix — -ulence

suffix — -ulence: fullness of (as in turbulence) (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: Latin ops meant 'wealth, power,' and -ulence names a fullness of something, as in turbulence -- so opulence is literally a fullness of wealth, richness visibly overflowing.

Use the root in a new word: opulent

Use the root in a new word: opulent: Opulent, the adjective form, describes something marked by opulence -- 'an opulent ballroom.'
